characterization_methods.key_findings: The as-cast plus homogenised 15Mn5Ni microstructure is two-phase (γ + B2); the micrograph shows a dark interdendritic network with a bright B2 second phase between the dendrite arms.
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural observation of the as-cast plus homogenised condition (and, for comparison, the hot-rolled condition)

characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Mn5Ni homogenised ingot composition (wt%): Mn 14.7, Al 9.8, C 0.9, Ni 4.1, Fe balance.
characterization_methods.purpose: Chemical composition analysis of the homogenised ingots (Table 1)
characterization_methods.technique: wet chemical method / standard emission spectroscopy

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Three austenitic LDS grades, including Fe-15Mn-9Al-5Ni-0.9C (15Mn5Ni), were prepared by vacuum induction melting; the defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots were used for further processing. Only the as-cast state is captured here.

Defect-free portions of the 30 kg ingots homogenised at 1423 K for two hours; this defines the as-cast plus homogenised (as-homogenised) condition of this sample, which is the precursor to hot rolling.

phases_present.morphology: bright second phase forming an interdendritic network between the dendrite arms

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase microstructure: austenite (γ) matrix with a bright B2 ordered second phase; the as-cast plus homogenised condition of 15Mn5Ni shows a dark interdendritic network with the bright second phase located between the dendrite arms.

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of the 15Mn5Ni homogenised ingot (Table 1, wt%): Mn 14.7, Al 9.8, C 0.9, Ni 4.1, Fe balance (analysed by wet chemical method/standard emission spectroscopy). [b0018, b0020, figure_unlabelled_002]

The B2 volume fraction of 15Mn5Ni was ~15% in the as-cast condition and decreased to ~12% after hot rolling at 1323 K, suggesting a possible B2 dissolution under hot-rolling conditions; the ~15% value corresponds to the as-cast/homogenised precursor state of this sample. [b0031]

Nickel addition makes the formation of the B2 phase more favourable at lower Mn content, so the 15Mn5Ni alloy contains a relatively higher volume fraction of B2 than 28Mn5Ni (~15% vs, respectively, lower values); this is the rationale given for the two-phase as-homogenised microstructure. [b0031]

This sample is the as-cast plus homogenised precursor condition (prior to hot rolling); the mechanical (hardness, nanoindentation, tensile), detailed TEM/ACOM/EBSD and fractography results reported in the paper are for the hot-rolled condition and therefore belong to a different (hot-rolled) sample, not to this as-homogenised sample. [b0018, b0022, b0023, b0025, b0035]
